title: OPAG-70: retire the digest gate, import the canonical operating block
summary: OPAG-70 step 1-2, now that OMARK-38 landed. This repo is public, so the operating block should never have lived here as content a public reader could see describes the fleet's private orchestration model -- the canonical import (@~/.claude/opum-fleet-operating.md) replaces the byte-identical inline copy every repo carried, retiring the pinned-digest CI check that existed only to catch drift between nine copies. One copy cannot drift from itself. Diffed the canonical file against this repo's current block before touching anything: the canonical file is genuinely ahead (reflects today's opum-marketplace/opum-fleet split in its own repo table, plus two new user-ruling sections dated 2026-09-09 -- mandatory AskUserQuestion formatting, a continuous-improvement standing duty) rather than stale or wrong, so the import resolves the diff automatically rather than needing manual reconciliation. Ruleset updated first: check . operating block digest dropped from main's required checks via gh api, verified by a fresh read, before the job or the inline block were touched.

acceptanceCriteria.text: main's require-ci-on-main ruleset no longer names check . operating block digest as a required check -- verified by re-reading the ruleset, done BEFORE the job or CLAUDE.md were touched, not after.
ci.yml's operating-block job is removed entirely.
CLAUDE.md's inline opum:fleet-operating:begin/end block is replaced with a single @~/.claude/opum-fleet-operating.md import line.
The canonical file was diffed against this repo's block before the swap, and the diff's nature (ahead vs. stale) was actually assessed, not skipped -- recorded in this task's own notes.

implementationNotes: Diff assessment, not skipped: canonical file (232 lines) vs this repo's prior inline block (174 lines) differ in two places -- the repo table row (now correctly shows opum-marketplace as public/lore+quest-only and a new opum-fleet row, reflecting OMARK-38) and two entirely new sections dated 'User ruling, 2026-09-09': AskUserQuestion is now mandatory for any user-facing decision, shaped as a two-option A/B with the recommendation named; and a standing 'continuous improvement' duty (capture corrections as rules not incidents, turn repetition into scripts/skills, ask why a gate didn't catch something sooner). Assessed as the canonical file being genuinely AHEAD of this repo's stale digest-pinned copy, not wrong or stale itself -- the import resolves this automatically rather than needing hand-reconciliation, and picks up whatever the canonical file says next time too.
finalSummary: Ruleset updated first (verified by fresh read), then ci.yml's operating-block job removed, then CLAUDE.md's 176-line inline block replaced with a single import line. Digest gate fully retired.
